target_customer: Inventors and small creators of physical products, and shoppers
problem: Kickstarter took work and rejected some projects; Swish let anyone list a product and handled the wholesale order and fulfillment.
business_model: Marketplace keeping 35 percent of product markup

founders.name: Iolanthe Chronis
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as Iolanthe Stronger; the surname conflict is unresolved.

competitors.name: Kickstarter
competitors.what: Crowdfunding platform taking 5 percent of funding totals
competitors.traction_then: Leading reward crowdfunding site; had rejected the founders' keychain product

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with listing windows and order management; the hard parts were operational (manufacturer orders, fulfillment).

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace with no stated network effects; larger crowdfunding sites could copy the model.

market_need_then: Founders said their own product was rejected by Kickstarter without explanation and described small creators as finding it too much work (TechCrunch, 2013-02).

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch coverage; the Swish name is used by several later unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Swish let anyone list a physical product for 30 days and then placed a single wholesale order, taking 35 percent of the markup and handling fulfillment itself. That meant holding inventory and shipping risk for a two person YC team, and Kickstarter and Indiegogo already owned the audience. No shutdown reason is public; the unit economics factor is an inference from the model and is low confidence.
notes: No website listed in the dataset (dead or unlisted). The 20K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, Swish Group, 2013-03-26, YC only) and its identity as this company is unconfirmed. YC page says Palo Alto/San Francisco; names differ between YC and TechCrunch. Cause of inactivity not public; failure factor is inferred.
